clue.text: Coleridge's salt of the earth? Not exactly!

definitions.text: Coleridge's salt of the earth? Not exactly!

parts.words: Coleridge's salt of the earth? Not exactly!
parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, and Coleridge's famous one in his long poem is very old; 'of the earth' is wrong only because he belongs to the sea

explanation.surface: Is Coleridge's poetic hero a down-to-earth, salt-of-the-earth type? Not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt of the earth' looks like the idiom for a decent ordinary person, but 'salt' is a sailor and 'Not exactly' admits he is of the sea, not the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem The Rime of the Ancient Mariner tells of an aged seaman, and an old sailor is a salt.

clue.text: Diplomat's wife in the morning gets fish on frock

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Diplomat's wife in the morning gets fish on frock (12)': AM + BASS + DRESS gives only AMBASSDRESS; the A of AMBASSADRESS has no clue word, so a word (likely 'a' before 'frock') seems missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Diplomat's wife in the morning gets fish on frock

clue.text: Escape from talk about the end of life

indicators.note: the word for talk goes about, i.e. around, the chosen letter

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of life

explanation.surface: A plea to dodge a lecture about mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E, the last letter of 'life', inside CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat death or fate is to escape it narrowly, so the verb serves as a synonym for escape.

clue.text: The issue is me going round a country

indicators.note: going round means the word me turns about and is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the trouble is a person touring a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem or a magazine number, but here it means something given off; 'going round' turns the first piece backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or flows out from a source, so it is an issue in that sense.

clue.text: Mortgage for a police dog?

definitions.meaning: a home loan whose rate follows the central bank's base rate
a dog trained to follow a scent trail for officers

explanation.walkthrough: A tracker mortgage is a British home loan that tracks the Bank of England base rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a base-rate-following home loan and a scent-following police animal are called by the same name.

clue.text: Strange chap swallows ale and jellyfish

indicators.note: swallows means the rearranged letters take the beer inside them
strange signals that the letters of chap are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd fellow downs beer and a jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the fodder to ACPH, and 'swallows' puts the beer inside, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acaleph is an old zoological name for a jellyfish or related sea creature.

clue.text: Fairy-tale wood — I must go first

indicators.note: must go first says the letter I is placed at the front of the charade

parts.note: taken as written
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: In a fairy-tale forest, someone insists on leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is softwood planks of fir or pine; 'must go first' puts I before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale situation is a perfect one, so as an adjective it means the same as perfect.

clue.text: Medium substance disturbs poet's calm

indicators.note: disturbs signals that the letters of poet's calm are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Something unsettles a poet's tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbs' rearranges the nine letters of POETS CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualist mediums were said to exude a ghostly substance during séances; that is its name.

clue.text: Whence comes bread from Holland?

indicators.note: comes from suggests the letters of bread are produced out of a source, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A question asking which Dutch place supplies bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The town's name is a rearrangement of BREAD, so whimsically it is where bread 'comes from'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is a city in the southern Netherlands, a Dutch place, i.e. somewhere in Holland.

clue.text: A mother otter turns to take the biscuit

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: turns signals that the letters of otter are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother otter twists round to snatch a cookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the biscuit' is an idiom, but here 'biscuit' alone is the definition; 'turns' makes RETTO from OTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An amaretto is an Italian almond macaroon, a kind of crisp biscuit.

clue.text: It's sweet to make love together, lying perhaps on the table

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert, the pudding course
to spoon is to kiss and cuddle romantically

explanation.surface: Someone thinks romance together is a treat, perhaps on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying perhaps on the table' looks like part of the amorous scene but is a definition by example of a piece of cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sized spoon is laid on the dining table as part of a place setting, so it is something lying there.

clue.text: It's a blow having a collection to retire!

parts.note: a set is a collection of things
to back away is to retreat, so back stands for retire

explanation.surface: Someone laments having to give up a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse or misfortune, which is what a blow means figuratively.

clue.text: Obscure conversion to pound pieces

indicators.note: conversion means the letters are changed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A financial note on changing coins into pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion to' rearranges L (pound) plus PIECES.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure it, as the moon blocks out the sun.

clue.text: A politician I must follow as an excuse

indicators.note: must follow says the letter I comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal, a member of a political party

explanation.surface: Someone explains that they must follow a politician, as a reason for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, and loosely any excuse.

clue.text: I'm placed at liberty if open to accusation

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter
put means placed
to be at liberty to do something is to be able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone says they are set free only if they can be charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imputable can be attributed or ascribed to someone as a fault, so it is open to accusation.

clue.text: Tramp wrapped in lots of papers holds lots of wine

indicators.note: wrapped in puts the vagrant inside the paper

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper, so reams are lots of papers
a hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: A vagrant swaddled in newspapers clutches a hoard of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' is used twice to different ends: REAMS of paper and large bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large champagne bottle holding six standard bottles, so several are a great deal of wine.

clue.text: Domineering older woman with engagement to cancel

parts.note: a battle is a military engagement
to axe a plan is to cancel it

explanation.surface: An overbearing older woman wants an engagement called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' looks matrimonial, fitting the woman, but it is a military clash.
explanation.definitionFit: Battleaxe is an informal, uncomplimentary term for a forceful, aggressive older woman.

clue.text: Apologetic, having five to split rent

indicators.note: to split means the number word breaks the rent apart from inside

parts.note: taken as written
penta is the Greek prefix for five

explanation.surface: Sorry, but you need five people to share the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone repentant feels regret for wrongdoing, much as an apologetic person does.

clue.text: "Man gone crazy" is my epithet

indicators.note: crazy signals the letters of man gone go wild into another order

explanation.surface: Someone says their nickname is 'Man gone crazy'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges MAN GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman naming an agnomen is an extra name or nickname, i.e. an epithet added for some achievement or trait.

clue.text: Suddenly grasp card game in a makeshift shelter

parts.note: to twig is to understand suddenly
loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: Understanding dawns over cards in a rough refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A twigloo is a woodland hut made of branches, a temporary shelter like that built by road protesters.

clue.text: Watch this! Married in the middle of a row!

indicators.note: in the middle of places the letter inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about a wedding happening amid a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or egg clock is a device to keep an eye on, so 'Watch this!' describes it whimsically.

clue.text: Record class gets smaller

parts.note: a set is a class or group of pupils
a figure going down is getting smaller

explanation.surface: A school class is shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down on paper is to record it in writing.

clue.text: They can be played with old bones, but not new

indicators.note: but not means a piece is to be left out

explanation.surface: Instruments that can be played with aged bones, though not fresh ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not new' removes N from O plus BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments, things a musician plays.

clue.text: Tranquillity, having lost a stone, becomes a complaint

indicators.note: having lost means a part is removed

parts.note: stillness is tranquillity
ST is the abbreviation for a stone in weight

explanation.surface: Calm turns to grievance after shedding weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment or disease in medical usage, so illness is a synonym.

clue.text: Hedge sparrows have such lips

indicators.note: have signals that the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Garden birds are said to have a certain kind of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'hEDGE Sparrows'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips are the edges or rims of things, like the lip of a cup or crater.

clue.text: Sailor goes to the opera with a pound, which is odd

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Norma is Bellini's opera
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A seaman attends the opera carrying a pound, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abnormal departs from the usual, which is what odd means.

clue.text: Problems with silver half-groats

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: half picks the first half of the word groats

explanation.surface: Trouble involving silver and old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A groat was an old English fourpenny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation, i.e. problems.

clue.text: "No port" response could be the call

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone imagines the reply 'No port' being the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NO PORT RESPONSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person-to-person telephone call is one made via an operator to a named individual.
